arm9_now_available.mapping: ARM9 is UNCOMPRESSED and maps 1:1 at 0x02000000, so file_offset = runtime_addr - 0x02000000. No BLZ step. ARM7 maps at 0x02380000. Verified by the peer against live emulator memory.

HP_UNITS_CORRECTION: HP is a u16 LITTLE-ENDIAN in 1/64 units. The "1/4 scale byte" in older docs is only the HIGH BYTE. Read 2 bytes at addr, not 1. Naruto 4-koma = 9216 raw = 144.0. Goku 10240 = 160.0. Luffy 9728 = 152.0. Anything reading one byte silently truncates - distrust prior sub-integer damage conclusions. Source: peer session, docs/research/HP-And-Damage-Runtime-Findings.md

k2b_results.pointer_gotcha: ability_t.bin relative pointer base = offset OF the pointer field, NOT after it (src/JUS.Tool/Texts/JusText.cs:90 evaluates Stream.Position before ReadInt32 advances). hp_findings.my_prediction_REFUTED: size*36 => size5=180 is dead. Harness read all 8 deck slots: every HP is an exact multiple of 64 raw / 8 displayed, and 180/8=22.5. HP carries no fraction; the 1/64 units exist for DAMAGE only, so the 1.250 hit is manufactured by the damage path and is not table data.

hp_findings.candidate: chr_b.bin has five u8 fields at 0x10, 0x14, 0x18, 0x1C, 0x20 (stride 4). ALL 370 of those bytes (74 x 5) are multiples of 8 - CONFIRMED, not coincidence. +16 is the dominant step (131 occurrences vs 63 zeros).
hp_findings.abilityId_indexes_chr_b: CONFIRMED by arithmetic: battle abilityId has 74 distinct values in 0..73, chr_b has 74 entries.
hp_findings.naruto_ladder: chr_b[20] = [144,160,176,144,144]; chr_b[24] (九尾) = [80,96,112,192,208]. Taking sizes 4/5/6 from entry20 slots 0/1/2 and sizes 7/8 from entry24 slots 3/4 gives 144,160,176,192,208 - a clean +16 ladder. 144 matches the harness RAM reading EXACTLY. Sizes 7-8 coming from a different chr_b entry also explains the komatxt rename to ナルト（九尾）, and 208 matches "8-koma have the most HP".
hp_findings.WEAKNESS: Only 19/74 entries are non-decreasing across the five slots (e.g. chr_b[66]=[104,64,152,64,224]). Either (A) slots are per-size HP but only the sizes a character owns are meaningful and the rest is filler, or (B) my stride-4 grouping is wrong and I am reading one byte from each of five different fields that happen to share the multiple-of-8 property. Reading these as u16 gives high bytes 1,4,5,16,20,22 (not constant), which favours B for the field boundaries. Confidence PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed.
hp_findings.FALSIFIABLE: Naruto size-5 panel (koma.bin record 502): mine says 160 (raw 10240), harness says 152 (raw 9728), my old guess said 180 (dead). One exact u16 read decides between two live hypotheses.
